To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hydrodynamic model of a vibrating hydrofoil is validated in case of forced motion, and in case of free motion.

(i) the fluid torque is a function of frequency and upstream velocity; (ii) it is possible to model the fluid torque in case of forced motion and (iii) the proposed model predicts correctly the fluid torque in the case of free motion.
the fluid structure interaction of a NACA 0.09 hydrofoil can be modeled by an added moment of mass, an added damping and an added stiffness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of numerical methods for the analysis of fluid-structure interaction problems, and the development of efficient computational algorithms for the solution of the governing equations.
numerical investigations of fluid structure interaction in the context of hydro elastic behavior.
the development of a numerical tool that can be used to predict the fluid-structure interaction of a vibrating blade in hydraulic machine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study is a first step in the investigation of the hydroelastic behaviour of a vibrating blade in hydraulic turbines and the model proposed can be used for further studies.
the present study is able to predict the behavior of an oscillating NACA 0006 hydrofoil in terms of fluid damping, fluid stiffness and added mass.
the proposed method is a reliable approach to identify hydro elastic coefficients of oscillating blades in hydraulic machines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model is capable of predicting the hydrodynamic behavior of oscillating hydrofoil in the frequency domain, which is a useful tool for the design of turbo machinery blades.
the fluid structure coupling can be successfully modeled in terms of a linear added mass, fluid damping and fluid stiffness.
a model for the hydro elastic behavior can be obtained through an investigation in case of forced motion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fluid structure coupling can be well modeled using the added mass and fluid damping, and that the fluid stiffness coefficient can be neglected.
the hydrodynamic coefficients can be accurately predicted by the numerical model, and the fluid stiffness coefficient is found to be of great importance in case of the forced oscillation.
the hydrodynamic moment can be accurately estimated using the proposed model.
